sections.title: Why this module matters
sections.body: Spring WebFlux interview questions test whether you understand reactive programming on the JVM — Mono vs Flux, backpressure, the Project Reactor operator vocabulary, Schedulers and threading, when reactive helps versus when it just adds complexity, and the migration patterns from blocking Spring MVC. This page is small but focused: each question is one a senior interviewer actually asks when WebFlux is on your resume.

sections.title: Mental model
sections.body:
WebFlux = **reactive streams** (`Mono`/`Flux`) on top of **Netty** by default.

- Mono = 0..1, Flux = 0..N, both **lazy**.
- **Backpressure** is the request-N protocol — consumers signal demand.
- **Schedulers** matter — `boundedElastic` for blocking, `parallel` for CPU.
- **Don't block** in a reactive chain; if you must, isolate with `subscribeOn(boundedElastic())`.

sections.title: Must-know concepts
sections.body:
The interview surface for this module breaks into these focus areas:

- **Backpressure** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.
- **Comparisons** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.
- **Error handling reactive** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.
- **Mono and flux** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.
- **R2dbc reactive data** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.
- **Reactive programming basics** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.
- **Spring webflux setup** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.
- **Testing reactive** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.
- **Scenario-based** — applied questions tying multiple topics together. Drill these *last*, after the fundamentals are sharp.

sections.title: Likely interview hooks
sections.body:
- **Reactive ≠ faster** — only wins on high-concurrency, IO-bound paths.
- **`switchMap` vs `flatMap`** — switch cancels prior, flatMap interleaves.
- **R2DBC vs JPA** — JPA is blocking; mixing kills the loop.
- **Testing** — `StepVerifier` for assertion, `WebTestClient` for HTTP.
- **Virtual threads make Webflux less compelling** for new projects — be ready to discuss the trade-off.

sections.title: Speaking template
sections.body: > *"I'd compose the pipeline as `Mono.fromX` → operators → `subscribe`, isolate any blocking call on `boundedElastic`, propagate context with `contextWrite`, and verify timing with `StepVerifier`. For new code I'd weigh WebFlux against virtual threads + plain blocking code."*
